I read p.133 (statement), p.134 (proof), pp.129-130 (A.5)-(A.13), and the Lean in SchedulePressure, PressureDatum, CorrectedPressureBounds, OutgoingHistories and OutgoingDilation. axisPressure d is (A.21) for the bump-free finalAngular, which equals P f(η) e^{y/10} on y ≤ 0 and matches the slope, interpolation, hold and tail stages. All six clauses are proved for every TailData and every real η, with analyticity on the strip |Im z| < 1/2, so the Lean implies the lemma. Both skeptics agreed and raised nothing new. I added the pairing skeptic's OutgoingHistories.Pi_eq_future_integral as the closest match to (A.23), and OutgoingDilation.axisDatum_unchanged for X_R-independence in physical coordinates. The three findings are encoding choices. I did not re-audit every Section A.2 stage; that belongs to Proposition A.4.

findings.summary: No single declaration states Lemma A.5. Its clauses are separate theorems about one object, SchedulePressure.axisPressure d, with (A.23) in CorrectedPressureBounds and OutgoingHistories. The lemma is their conjunction.
X_R-independence is stated as translation invariance of the log-coordinate integral, for every real X_R, including X_R ≤ 0 where Real.log is a junk value. The Lean profile has no X_R parameter.
(A.23) is stated in y = log(X/X_R) for every ResetWitness, not in X for one fixed complete profile. The ODE Π_X = E²/(2X) appears as d/dy Π = E²/2.
